name: Zanzibar · Stone Town
tagline: Swahili history before the island coast
summary: Treat Stone Town as a destination alongside a Zanzibar beach stay or northern-Tanzania safari. Walk its carved-door lanes with context, visit the slavery memorial, eat Swahili dishes and allow a separate day for a forest or island excursion.
seasonNote: Warm and humid year-round. The long rains commonly affect March–May; boat plans depend on the daily sea forecast.
arrival: Abeid Amani Karume airport is south of Stone Town. Prearrange the hotel transfer and the final meeting point because many lanes are pedestrian-only. Ferries also link Dar es Salaam.
gettingAround: Explore the old town on foot. Use arranged road transfers for Jozani or beach areas and licensed boats for island excursions.
cashTip: Carry a modest amount of local cash for small purchases; use cards where accepted and check menu or ticket prices before paying.
foodTip: Try pilau, coconut-based dishes and fresh juice. Book rooftop dinners ahead and explain vegetarian or halal requirements directly.
buyTip: Buy spices in sealed labelled packs, kanga textiles and locally made craft; check your destination’s import rules for food and natural materials.
baseArea: Stone Town for heritage and food; add a separate coast base if swimming and beaches are a major goal.

connections.note: Combine with a northern-Tanzania safari; confirm whether the flight uses Arusha or Kilimanjaro airport.
Planning air time only; schedules and airport connections must be checked.

items.summary: Carved doors, coral-stone buildings and winding lanes reveal centuries of Swahili trading history.
items.expect: African, Arab, Indian and European influences appear together in the town’s street pattern and architecture.
items.tip: A guide is optional extra spending; heat, uneven lanes and requests for photographs call for an unhurried approach.
